$comment: Evidence specs for the agent skill, one per runbook question ID (data-key in content/index.html). scripts/build-skill.mjs joins these with the question text, lever and track read from index.html; verify-skill.mjs fails on an unmapped question or an orphan spec. evidence: what in a workspace answers the question. in: glob sets to search. patterns: case-insensitive regexes, matched per line. ask: usually only the user can answer (org process, billing, habits); search anyway, then ask.

qsh-q1.evidence: Which meter the coding agent runs on: Bedrock tokens (agent configured for Amazon Bedrock), Kiro credits, or a plan allowance.

qsh-q2.evidence: Documented behaviour at the limit: Bedrock throttling, a Kiro credit block, or overage.

qsh-q3.evidence: Alarms or alerts on Bedrock quota or token use, or on credit use, before the limit.

rsm-q1.evidence: Committed, shared agent settings that set the default model.

rsm-q2.evidence: Subagent definitions that set their own model and reasoning effort.

rsm-q3.evidence: A default reasoning-effort or thinking setting at low or moderate, with deep reasoning by exception.

rsm-q4.evidence: Pinned model IDs in shared config, and a documented trial and retirement-audit process.

seat-q1.evidence: A seat-usage audit and removal of inactive seats; usually only the user knows.

seat-q2.evidence: Kiro plan tiers matched to usage, or a shared credit pool; usually only the user knows.

scap-q1.evidence: Spend broken down by user, team and department: agent telemetry, per-team inference profiles, cost allocation tags.

scap-q2.evidence: Organisation spend caps and per-user limits that are enforced: gateway budgets, Kiro limits, AWS Budgets actions.

scap-q3.evidence: A documented way to request more quota, with a named approver and turnaround.

mcc-q1.evidence: An inventory of optional agent features that raise token use (agent teams, 1M context, scheduled tasks).

mcc-q2.evidence: Managed or shared settings that switch those features off centrally.

mop-q1.evidence: A committed baseline of approved MCP servers and skills at org, team or project level.

mop-q2.evidence: A security, supply-chain and data-handling review for third-party agent tooling.

owm-q1.evidence: Benchmarks of cost per solved task for open-weight model and harness pairs on the team's own tasks.

owm-q2.evidence: The gateway and data path to the open-weight model: in-account Bedrock or a third-party API.

owm-q3.evidence: A check that tool calling works through the gateway into the harness in use.

dedu-q1.evidence: A living org guide for the coding agent: setup, constraints and why, session practice, how to raise a limit.

dedu-q2.evidence: Onboarding that installs and configures the agent with org, team and repo settings on day one.

dedu-q3.evidence: Pair or mob programming with the agent, and use of existing external courses.

dedu-q4.evidence: Sponsored AI champions and a community of practice.

msc-q1.evidence: Guidance to reset context between unrelated tasks rather than wait for compaction.

msc-q2.evidence: Use of rewind or checkpoints to undo an agent change.

msc-q3.evidence: A habit of finding what fills the context before resetting a session.

rpt-q1.evidence: Guidance to name files by path instead of open-ended exploration.

ivs-q1.evidence: Large command output kept out of the main session: filtering, output limits, delegated analysis.

ail-q1.evidence: Small always-loaded instruction files, with occasional workflows loaded on demand.

msc-q4.evidence: A periodic review that removes unused MCP servers.

msc-q5.evidence: A habit of picking model and effort before the first prompt.

mre-q1.evidence: Reasoning effort chosen by task difficulty and validated on representative work.

mre-q2.evidence: Deep reasoning escalated by exception only.

pbe-q1.evidence: Plan-then-execute as the default for non-trivial work: plan mode, specs.

pbe-q2.evidence: Plans that name tests, checks, review criteria and a stopping condition.

kwys-q1.evidence: Spend decomposed into its terms: token usage read from responses, Bedrock metrics, budgets, bill reviews.

kwys-q2.evidence: Cost per successful task measured, and a release gate on it.

kwys-q3.evidence: Attribution: per-team accounts, application inference profiles, cost allocation tags, request metadata.

rtm-q1.evidence: Which models are called for which requests, and any routing to a cheaper model.

rtm-q2.evidence: Pinned model IDs and an audit of them against the Bedrock lifecycle pages.

rtp-q1.evidence: Batch inference jobs or service tiers chosen per workload, versus synchronous on-demand calls.

rtp-q2.evidence: Cross-region inference profile IDs (us., eu., apac., global.) rather than single-Region model IDs.

cwr-q1.evidence: Prompt caching enabled (cache points) with the stable system prompt and tools first.

cwr-q2.evidence: Cache hits verified and tracked: cache read and write token counts, invocation logging.

cwr-q3.evidence: A cache TTL chosen to match how often sessions call.

eff-q1.evidence: Reasoning effort or thinking budget set per type of step, not left at the model default.

eff-q2.evidence: Output tokens per successful task compared before an effort change.

dis-q1.evidence: Invocation volume against the distillation or self-hosting break-even.

dis-q2.evidence: The managed, managed-compute or self-managed path chosen deliberately.

dis-q3.evidence: Curated training data, an A/B test of the student, and a refresh plan.

sp-q1.evidence: The system prompt: where it is built and how large it is.

sp-q2.evidence: A versioned system prompt with no per-call values (dates, IDs) that break the cache.

csl-q1.evidence: Context per request measured and budgeted: token counts, limits, truncation.

crs-q3.evidence: Tool and runtime outputs bounded before they enter the context.

rag-q1.evidence: The vector store and its pricing model against query volume.

rag-q2.evidence: Retrieval sized to the question: result count, chunk size, reranking.

rag-q3.evidence: Re-syncs that embed only changed documents.

csl-q2.evidence: How conversation history is kept: append-only, windowed, summarised, or a memory store.

csl-q3.evidence: History pruned at natural boundaries without breaking the cache every turn.

crs-q1.evidence: A costed inventory of tools, skills and MCP servers.

crs-q2.evidence: Each call sent only the tools it needs.

bso-q1.evidence: Agent loops with termination and retry limits.

bso-q2.evidence: Multi-agent designs, and whether they beat a single agent.

bso-q3.evidence: Workflow cost measured end to end, including retries and coordination.

ceb-q1.evidence: Bounded concurrency, queue depth and fan-out in dispatcher code.

ceb-q2.evidence: Request, token and connection limits per caller at the gateway.

teui-q1.evidence: Every model and tool call traceable to its caller and task: request metadata, tracing, invocation logging.

teui-q2.evidence: Invocations reconciled against requested work to find orphans.

teui-q3.evidence: Alerts on calls with no task, after completion, or over budget.

psr-q1.evidence: An interface or template that asks for output, constraints and scope before the agent starts.

guid-q1.evidence: Clickable options in the interface instead of only a blank text box.

guid-q2.evidence: Low-variance inputs (choices, validation) so clarifying round-trips are rare.

cost-q1.evidence: The interface shows users what their session costs.

cost-q2.evidence: That cost shown during the session, while the user can still act.
